_comment: Accepted mismatch counts for metadata/check_release_consistency.py. A check fails when its count goes UP. Lower an entry when you fix something; never raise one to let a release through. `schema` is 0 because the 88 stale column lists it found were repaired when the check was written, and `corrections-resolve` is 0 because every identifier does resolve once the comparison is done right; `counts` and `corrections-pinned` are 0 from 2026-10-24: the 59 contradicted rows were refreshed (#3214, #3213) and all 92 unpinned corrections were placed in their release (#3216). The two withdrawal entries are the remaining October 2026 backlog. `unexplained-repeats` enters at 40 on 2026-10-25: a published density above 1 with no occasion column, which is proof of a duplicate id-item pair that nothing explains. It started at 68 and 32 of those were stale rows, refreshed in the same commit (sris_silvia2022 published 221 participants against 1,192 live); the 40 that remain are real duplicates and real data defects, triaged on #3222 -- 22 of them one id covering two respondents, the rest trial-level tasks whose trial column was dropped at ingest, plus two simsyn tables whose repeats are by construction. Lower it as the data is fixed, table by table. `withdrawals-records` drops 338 -> 147 on 2026-10-28: the item-text half of it was the 191 withdrawn rows `itemtext_metadata` kept, and #3240 pruned them, so every remaining hit is a withdrawn table still carrying a `biblio` row. The one item-text hit left (FomoNegativeAffect_cremer_2026_panas) is NOT baselined, because it is a live rights exposure rather than an accepted mismatch: it closes when the withdrawal is applied and released, and `withdrawals-live` is deliberately left at 38 so that run fails until it is.
